extracted.intended_audience: researchers, Indigenous community partners, and grant writers planning Indigenous-led, community-engaged research
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study/preregistration describing a three-day Indigenous-led Grant Planning Retreat and its evaluation; focuses on documenting processes, conditions, and best practices to support culturally safe, Indigenous-led research and collaborative grant writing. Useful for teams planning Indigenous-led, community-engaged grants and for evaluating such retreats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Indigenous-led, culturally safe research
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance cultural safety through Indigenous-led research and knowledge mobilization; prioritize collaboration and relationship building across law, corrections, and mental health services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center Indigenous leadership, ensure research is led by Indigenous people, and design activities (e.g., retreats) to support culturally safe outcomes rather than imposing external frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimagine research through Indigenous leadership, ceremony, and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimagine research through Indigenous leadership, ceremony, and relationships by creating unique spaces (e.g., a healing lodge) that support Indigenous ways of knowing and being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ceremony and relationship-building as active components of research design and planning (e.g., hosting retreats at culturally meaningful sites; involving Elders and Knowledge Keepers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relational, cultural, and structural conditions for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore what relational, cultural, and structural conditions made the Grey Buffalo Grandfather Lodge effective for advancing Indigenous-led research and working collaboratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate physical setting, cultural supports, relational dynamics, and organizational/structural arrangements that facilitated (or hindered) Indigenous-led collaboration; use qualitative methods to document these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the Indigenous-led research process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document roles, decision-making processes, protocols, and steps taken to ensure research leadership and governance are Indigenous-led; include practical account of day-to-day processes used during planning and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify best practices for Indigenous-led partnerships and knowledge mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify best practices to inform future Indigenous-led research partnerships and community-engaged knowledge mobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize lessons and actionable recommendations from the retreat that other teams can adopt when forming partnerships, planning grants, and mobilizing knowledge back to communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Indigenous methodologies grounded in meaningful relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Indigenous-led research processes and Indigenous methodologies grounded in meaningful relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize methodologies that foreground relationality, reciprocity, and Indigenous epistemologies rather than solely Western research paradigms; center community relationships in methodological choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize relational accountability and Indigenous protocols in dissemination and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings will be shared in ways that prioritize relational accountability and Indigenous protocols, ensuring that communities have authority in data interpretation and use (Global Indigenous Data Alliance, 2020; First Nations Information Governance, 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Indigenous data governance principles (e.g., GIDA/FNIG), involve community partners in interpretation and decisions about data use, and ensure outputs respect cultural protocols and community authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge mobilization bridging scholarship and community
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge mobilization strategies will effectively bridge the gap between scholarly research and community, aligned with principles of scholar-activism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design dissemination and mobilization plans that translate academic findings into community-relevant formats, prioritize community benefit, and engage scholar-activist approaches to ensure research uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods data collection appropriate to aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a mixed-method approach of an online survey or semi-structured interviews to qualitatively explore retreat outcomes and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ flexible qualitative methods (surveys and semi-structured interviews) suited to capturing relational and contextual data; justify method choices in relation to exploring cultural and structural conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate retreat effectiveness in promoting Indigenous-led, culturally safe research
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the effectiveness of the Grant Planning Retreat in promoting Indigenous-led, culturally safe research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the retreat advanced goals such as Indigenous leadership in planning, strengthened relationships across jurisdictions, and produced actionable plans for a national grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive composition of participants and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring together Elders and Knowledge Keepers, Indigenous trainees, community partners, individuals with lived experience of incarceration, academics, practitioners, and decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure participant diversity across roles and jurisdictions to support relational accountability, breadth of perspectives, and relevance to multiple systems (law, corrections, mental health).
